On the earnings call, CEO Elon Musk said a merger with Tesla , his automaker, would be a "good idea," adding that the boards of both companies have formed special committees to discuss a tie-up. Tesla reports third-quarter results after the bell on Wednesday. Here's how SpaceX did compared to LSEG consensus estimates: Revenue: $14.58 billion vs. $12.72 billion expected Earnings per share: 45 cents adjusted vs. 13 cents expected SpaceX said in a release that it recorded operating income of $2.8 billion and net income of $4.4 billion. In the same period a year earlier, SpaceX reported a net loss of $1.05 billion. CFO Bret Johnsen said on the call that revenue in the first quarter of 2027 will be $33 billion to $37 billion, trouncing the average $22.2 billion average analyst estimate, according to LSEG. Johnsen attributed the forecast to "increased visibility into our compute contract pipeline over the next six months." While SpaceX is best known for its reusable rockets, most of its revenue and profit in recent quarters came from the company's connectivity segment, which consists of its Starlink satellite internet service. Starlink's subscribers base grew to 13.6 million in the quarter, up from 12 million in the prior period. Total connectivity revenue jumped 69% to $5.25 billion from $3.1 billion a year earlier. Analysts were expecting $4.84 billion, according to StreetAccount. Revenue from consumer Starlink subscribers amounted to $3.12 billion, while the company generated $2.13 billion from government and enterprise customers. Buzz has been building about Starlink's plans to build a U.S. mobile network after SpaceX, earlier this month, announced that it's buying 800 MHz of low-band spectrum, and after the Federal Communications Commission approved a plan for the company to build out a 15,000-satellite constellation. SpaceX jumped into AI with the purchase earlier this year of xAI, Musk's AI lab. The company has been rapidly expanding that business by renting out capacity to Google , Anthropic and others. AI, which SpaceX now calls "Super Intelligence," has emerged as its largest business. Revenue jumped ninefold to $7.56 billion from $813 million in the same quarter last year. Analysts expected sales of $6.47 billion, according to StreetAccount. During the third quarter, SpaceX also closed its $60 billion purchase of AI coding startup Cursor. Meanwhile, SpaceX's launch business was up just slightly in the quarter, with sales rising to $1.77 billion from $1.67 billion a year ago. Almost all of SpaceX's profit still comes from Starlink. Operating income in the connectivity unit about doubled to $2.37 billion. The AI business swung to a profit of $431 million, while the space division lost $7 million. Between infrastructure, cloud deals and paying users of the Grok AI models and products, Musk said on the call that annual recurring revenue by the end of next year will be between $500 billion and $1 trillion. Analysts are projecting full-year 2027 revenue of about $110 billion, according to LSEG, which would be up more than 100% from this year. 11 Hours Ago SpaceX generated revenue of $1.77 billion from launches watch now VIDEO 5:47 05:47 SpaceX shares continue to climb on Q3 beat Fast Money SpaceX's launch business generated $1.77 billion in revenue in the third quarter. The company touted its Starship Flight 14 as a major milestone on the earnings call, and Musk said SpaceX will attempt to "catch both the booster and the ship," during its next test flight of the massive rocket. He added that SpaceX has a "steady stream of Starship flight attempts" scheduled through the end of this year, and accelerating next year. The company recently announced plans to build a $100 billion spaceport in Louisiana. SpaceX COO Gwynne Shotwell said on the call that SpaceX aims to conduct its first launch from the facility by 2029. Musk said the first launch may be possible by the end of 2028. 11 Hours Ago SpaceX must face NAACP lawsuit over air pollution in Memphis area The U.S. Department of Justice lost its bid to have a federal court in Mississippi toss a lawsuit filed by the NAACP against SpaceX alleging Clean Air Act violations by Musk's company in the Memphis area. The DOJ had accused the NAACP of threatening "American national, economic, and energy security" by asking the court to temporarily shut off of the power supply used by SpaceX at its Colossus data centers. The data centers are powered by methane gas-burning turbines, installed by SpaceX's AI business. The NAACP, in its suit, said Musk's company built and used gas-burning turbines for power without first obtaining proper permits, and without installing required pollution controls. In the court's order, published Tuesday , a judge wrote there was "no 'fairly possible' interpretation of the Clean Air Act that would give the United States the right to unilaterally dismiss a citizen suit." 14 Hours Ago Musk says Tesla-SpaceX merger would be 'good idea' A fleet of Tesla Cyber trucks is parked at charging stations outside the SpaceX launch production facility in Starbase, Texas, U.S., July 20, 2026. Steve Nesius | Reuters Musk said the boards at Tesla and SpaceX have formed special committees to discuss a potential merger "at the request of shareholders," noting that these groups "consist of independent directors." Because Musk is a "conflicted party," he said he can't be in the discussions. "I do think there's a lot of merit to combining the companies as we are pretty much in the superintelligence singularity, and there's a lot to be gained from cooperating," Musk said, referring to the development of software, chips and more. "Do I think it would be a good idea? Yes," Musk said. "But at the end of the day, the shareholders have to be supportive of this." Musk said that on the Tesla side, "we will need a 50% vote of all shares -- not just those who vote -- but of all shareholders, and that's quite a high hurdle." Musk thanked ASML and other suppliers for prioritizing equipment deliveries for the factory. SpaceX secured significant tax incentives in June for the facility despite local opposition from residents concerned about the strain on local resources. —Lora Kolodny 15 Hours Ago Musk ordered restrictions on Starlink in Ukraine, according to WSJ watch now VIDEO 1:53 01:53 Ukraine’s Zelenskyy criticizes President Trump’s decision to suspend new sanctions on Russia Squawk on the Street According to a report from the Wall Street Journal on Tuesday, Musk ordered restrictions on the use of Starshield , a military-grade version of Starlink, in Ukraine in recent weeks, impeding some military operations and the country's ability to defend against intensifying attacks by Russia. Intuitive Surgical earned $3 per share, excluding certain items, on revenue of $3.05 billion. SpaceX — Shares gained 8% after the Elon Musk-led rocket company reported a 161% jump in third-quarter revenue to $14.58 billion. Musk also said that SpaceX and Tesla , his auto manufacturer, have formed special committees to discuss a merger. Tesla shares were up 1%. Space stocks — Other aerospace companies were higher following SpaceX's earnings jump. Rocket Lab rose 2.5%, while AST SpaceMobile was higher by almost 3%. Firefly Aerospace jumped 3.5%. Netflix — Shares of Netflix fell almost 7% after the streaming giant reported third-quarter revenue that was in line with Wall Street's expectations. Sales came in at $12.87 billion, up 12% year over year, boosted by growth in membership and an increase in subscription prices that went into effect in March, the company said. AT & T — The telecommunications company slid 3.5% despite reporting an earnings and revenue beat in its third-quarter financial report. Dell was jumping by 5.5%, while HPE rose 4.5%. Revenue came in at $6.55 billion, compared to analysts polled by FactSet's expectation for $6.56 billion. Adjusted earnings, however, beat estimates, and the company raised its full-year guidance for the metric. Philip Morris International — The tobacco and consumer goods company slipped 1% after it reported better-than-expected results in its third-quarter earnings report. However, full-year 2026 earnings guidance came in below expectations, according to analysts polled by FactSet. — CNBC's Deena Zaidi, Fred Imbert and Scott Schnipper contributed reporting.

headlines.article_text: Nvidia announces Vera Rubin racks that can be shipped on a truck Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Nvidia's new DSX Pod AI Factory packages seven Vera Rubin AI racks in a shipping container designed to be transported by truck. All the cabling and liquid cooling for the Pod are assembled at the factory. Nvidia did not disclose a price; analysts estimate a single Vera Rubin rack can cost more than $7 million. In this article NVDA Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Co-founder, President and CEO of US technology company Nvidia, Jensen Huang, gestures during a press briefing in Paris on Oct. 13, 2026. Joel Saget | AFP | Getty Images Nvidia announced Wednesday a new product that will put seven of its Vera Rubin AI racks into a shipping container, the company's latest effort to move up the stack and offer complete systems for artificial intelligence computing. The DSX Pod AI Factory is roughly the size of a standard shipping container and weighs about 28,000 kilograms, Nvidia said. It's designed to be shipped on a truck on normal roads and all the cabling and liquid cooling for the Pod are assembled at the factory, the company said. "The only thing that has to happen when it gets to the site is it's placed in its location, connected to the rest of the other containers, and validated through final burning and testing," Nvidia VP of hyperscale computing Ian Buck said on a call with reporters this week. DSX Pod AI factory will reduce the time for a new AI data center to start serving tokens from six months to 14 days, according to the company. Nvidia said the pod is intended for customers worldwide and could help address deployment challenges faced by European customers. Nvidia did not announce a price for the system, but analysts say a single Vera Rubin rack can cost over $7 million. The DSX Pod is a reference design that will ship from Nvidia's manufacturing partners. Nvidia said it was working with manufacturers including Foxconn, Gigabyte, Lenovo, HPE, Quanta, and Pegatron. Nvidia expects deliveries to start in early 2027. Nvidia, once a chip company, now offers networking, storage, and other data center needs to its customers. Its AI systems have evolved from single GPU chips to servers with four or eight GPUs, then to entire racks and now to the DSX Pod, a containerized building block with several racks already integrated. "What we offer into one gigawatt went from about $18 billion or so per gigawatt, to $20-something billion per gigawatt, to now $40-plus billion per gigawatt," Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said recently on a podcast. Gigawatts refer to the size of data center infrastructure by how much power is used. "My sense is that's going to keep going up." headlines.title: House committee says Webull messages point to China access to U.S. customer data
headlines.summary: The House Select Committee on China earlier this month said online investing platform Webull is quietly "tied in structural ways" to China's government.
headlines.article_text: Webull U.S. customer data access in China questioned Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points The House Select Committee on China says internal Webull messages from 2021 indicate that an employee believed to be in China had access to information about a U.S. customer account. Webull, which is an online investing platform, has said sensitive U.S. customer data is restricted to U.S.-based employees An Oct. 7 report by the select committee found that Webull is quietly "tied in structural ways" to China's government, representing a national security threat to American finance. In this article BULL Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT watch now VIDEO 2:46 02:46 House committee says Webull messages point to China access to U.S. customer data Squawk Box Internal messages between employees of online investing platform Webull suggest a company employee in China had access to information about a U.S. customer, despite the company having said it bars such sharing, according to an analysis of the messages by the House Select Committee on China . The analysis comes nearly two weeks after CNBC first detailed the bipartisan select committee's report that concluded that Webull, which counts 28 million users, is quietly "tied in structural ways" to China's government, representing a national security threat to American finance. Webull shares slid more than 19% on the heels of that Oct. 7 report. At the time of the report, Webull told CNBC in a statement that "U.S. customer data is stored in the U.S. and access to sensitive customer data is controlled by the U.S." But the newly released internal messages by the House Select Committee on China, which CNBC exclusively obtained, raise questions about whether that has always been the case. The committee has focused on threats posed by China and protecting U.S. industry from Chinese competition. One message thread suggests a Webull employee was in China during a discussion about a U.S. customer account. The thread also indicates the account was previously approved by a China Webull team member and an American counterpart. The messages, dating to 2021, were sent on Microsoft Teams between Brendan Fuller, a manager at Webull's U.S. brokerage, and an employee named Zhenghan Wang, whose nickname is "Rock." The select committee says Wang was likely in China at the time. In one message, Fuller messaged Wang about concerns involving a particular trading account. "We saw these problems ... and approve account," Fuller wrote. Wang replied: "Yes,CIP." CIP is an acronym for Customer Identification Program, a U.S. regulatory requirement that financial institutions verify the identities of individuals and entities opening accounts. "I thought so," Fuller responded. Wang asked Fuller: "Who approve the account?" Fuller responded: "One China team member and one US team." Wang then asked: "I want to know in what situation (CIP), can we approve the account open?" Fuller responded: "I think we just approve them all no matter what ..." "And then we pay for vendors. And create report and work," Fuller added. Wang then replied that "CIP=" followed by Mandarin Chinese characters forming a common phrase that translates as "Exists in name only," or "Useless." A spokesperson for the select committee, in a statement to CNBC, said, "All the evidence in these text messages points to Zhenghan Wang, a Webull employee, being located in China with access to U.S. customer data at the time he worked for the company." An analysis by the committee concluded that Wang was in China at the time of the exchange because the messages' time stamps indicated that Wang was working daytime hours in Beijing, and because he set his software to translate the messages into simplified Chinese. A Webull spokesperson did not directly respond to CNBC's questions about Wang's access to U.S. customer data in 2021 and whether that disproved the company's assertion that its U.S. data does not go to China. The Webull spokesperson said, "Protecting customer data is central to Webull's operations." "Webull's U.S. customer data is stored only in the U.S. on AWS servers in Virginia and Oregon, with access to sensitive data restricted to U.S.-based employees," the spokesperson said. "U.S. broker-dealer operations are directed exclusively by U.S.-based personnel, and no individuals based outside the U.S. have ever exercised operational or decision-making authority over Webull's U.S. broker-dealer business." The company spokesperson also criticized the select committee's release of the messages. "The Teams messages now being referenced date back to a 2021 routine FINRA matter, which was concluded," the spokesperson said. FINRA, or the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority, is the self-regulatory organization for member broker-dealers. Read more CNBC politics and policy coverage Trump waives broad new Russia sanctions and tariffs under Graham Act 2026 midterms money race: Democrats surge as Musk backs Republicans Why Trump and GOP's billion-dollar midterm election blitz isn't working The messages' "recent disclosure, alongside the Select Committee's report relying on preliminary and outdated information, raises legitimate questions about the timing and circumstances surrounding their release," Webull's spokesperson said. "Webull rejects irresponsible speculation and stands on our well-documented record: Webull's data protection practices are robust, continuously enhanced, and independently verified." The select committee's Oct. 7 report argued that Webull's corporate structure means the firm's "software development, data pipelines, and core engineering operations" are dependent on infrastructure subject directly to Beijing's laws. Those Chinese laws can compel firms to cooperate with the government in various ways, including mandating data transfers. The select committee on Tuesday issued a press release titled, "The Facts on Webull's Ties to China." The release said that since the committee issued its report, Webull "has ... responded with numerous false statements about its business and its interactions with the Select Committee." The committee listed five claims by Webull, followed by what the committee labeled "The Truth." One section, titled "Webull Claim: 'U.S. customer data is stored in the U.S.,'" was followed by a rebuttal that said, "The Truth: The Select Committee's report does not dispute where the data is stored. "Its finding is about who can reach the data and the systems that process it," the committee continued. "The report found that Webull affiliate Webull Technologies Limited previously used Tencent Cloud, a China-based provider, to host certain user data ... Webull has not said what data Tencent hosted or when that ended." Webull said Tuesday that it was partnering with Kalshi , the prediction market platform, to offer so-called perpetual futures to U.S. customers. The first set of perpetual futures, which do not have an expiration date, as traditional futures do, would be for cryptocurrencies, Webull said. Win McNamee | Getty Images SpaceX jumped in premarket trading on Wednesday after the company reported surging revenue growth in its third quarter, and owner Elon Musk floated a potential SpaceX- Tesla merger. The space company, which made its debut on the Nasdaq in the biggest IPO ever in June, reported third-quarter revenue on Tuesday of $14.6 billion, up 161% from the previous year, and beating LSEG consensus estimates of $12.72 billion. Meanwhile, its operating income from operations came in at $2.8 billion, with net income of $4.4 billion, after reporting a net loss of $1.05 billion in the same period a year earlier. On the earnings call, Musk said he's considering a combination with Tesla — which would mark the largest merger in history — and that the boards of both companies have created specific committees to discuss a consolidation. "I do think there's a lot of merit to combining the companies as we are pretty much in the superintelligence singularity, and there's a lot to be gained from cooperating," Musk said on the call. Tesla is set to report third-quarter earnings after the closing bell on Wednesday. SpaceX shares last rose 8.5% before the markets opened on Wednesday. Meanwhile, Tesla shares were up 1.4% in premarket trading. Shares of other space stocks, including Rocket Lab , Intuitive Machines , and AST SpaceMobile , were all higher in premarket trading. SpaceX shares since its debut on the Nasdaq. SpaceX forecasts first-quarter 2027 revenue between $33 billion and $37 billion, beating the average analyst estimate of $22.2 billion, per LSEG. "We delivered another strong quarter in Q3. Revenue grew an impressive 161% year-over-year, fueled by continued momentum in Connectivity and a clear inflection in our Super Intelligence business," SpaceX's Chief Financial Officer Bret Johnson said in the earnings release. Johnson pinned the strong results on recurring revenue from its satellite internet business, Starlink , and significant expansion of its Super Intelligence [SI] infrastructure. The company has dived into AI this year, which it's now calling SI. The segment is its largest business unit, with revenue soaring ninefold to $7.56 billion from $813 million in the same quarter last year. Bull case for AI cloud providers Commentary on computing during the earnings call supported "continued pricing power and shorter payback periods" for AI cloud providers, Truist Securities analysts said in a Tuesday note. The analysts said Coreweave and Nebius are set to benefit and capture demand as "pricing power will more than offset higher rates."
